3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Early in the morning, I heard a soft tap on the door to my bedchambers.

5.speaker: Player_Romus
5.text: "Go away. I don't have to be up for another hour."

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: Bruno jumped off my bed, ran to the door and began scratching at it. It didn't open.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: Bruno ran to the door and began scratching at it. It didn't open.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: There was no reply, just another soft knock.

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: There were a few seconds of silence, then another soft knock.

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: I dragged myself out of bed and walked towards the door.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: As I was about to open it, I noticed an object had been slipped underneath it.

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text:
"Find me in the labyrinth of past memories, 

left at the crossroads of whispering trees.

Close to the heart, all wrongs become right,

as we forge ahead from shadow into light.

Retracing our steps, we can find what we missed

The words left unsaid, the lips left unkissed."

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: I looked out the window. The sky had just barely begun to lighten, and a grey mist still hung over the palace gardens.

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: My eyes came to rest on the hedge maze. I remembered watching Pabel and his father construct it when I was a teenager.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Bruno followed me out of my bedroom. I ran into Titus pacing up and down the hallway.

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: I walked out of my bedroom and ran straight into Titus. My guard was pacing up and down the hallway.

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: "I'm going for a walk. No need to accompany me."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: "Who was at my door just now?"

33.speaker: Titus Gordion
33.text: "The palace grounds are secure, Your Majesty. Enjoy."

34.speaker: Titus Gordion
34.text: "Your butler, Your Majesty. I told him to return at your appropriate wake-up time."

35.speaker: Titus Gordion
35.text: "Not since Derdia. I can't believe I let you down like that."

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: Few other palace staff were about as I wandered into the mist-enshrouded gardens.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: Bruno split off to chase a squirrel as I made my way to the maze. Its entrance was marked by a pair of willow trees.

61.speaker: Narrator
61.text: Pabel was sitting there, waiting for me. He reached his hand towards mine.

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: "It was a lovely poem. But between the war and everything else going on, I'm really not in the mood."

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: I made my way to the maze. Its entrance was marked by a pair of willow trees.

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "It was a lovely poem. But considering everything that's been going on, I'm not really in the mood."

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: He gave a brief sigh of disappointment and withdrew his hand.

86.speaker: Pabel Adria
86.text: "It's fine. We can talk for a few minutes."

87.speaker: Pabel Adria
87.text: "Your royal visit to Derdia is coming up, isn't it? How are the preparations going?"

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: I took a seat on the ground next to him. He turned to look into my eyes.

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: By the time we finally spoke, the morning sunlight was peeking through the branches above us.

93.speaker: Titus Gordion
93.text: "Not since the events in Wehlen. I can't believe I let you down like that."

94.speaker: Titus Gordion
94.text: "Your butler was just here. Should I fetch him?"

97.speaker: Player_Romus
97.text: "No need. I'm just going for a quick walk."

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "Keep guarding my room. I'll be back shortly."

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: Pabel gave a short laugh. He sat up and plucked a leaf out of my hair.

106.speaker: Player_Romus
106.text: "Do you think Titus knows about us yet?"

107.speaker: Pabel Adria
107.text: "He's got eyes everywhere. But if he were able to pin something on me yet, he would have."

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: Pabel sat up and plucked a leaf out of my hair.

112.speaker: Pabel Adria
112.text: "He knows we're friends. I doubt any other possibility has penetrated his skull."

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: He reached into the pocket of his suit jacket and pulled out a newspaper clipping.

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: His suit jacket was lying on the ground behind us. He reached into its pocket and pulled out a newspaper clipping.

119.speaker: Pabel Adria
119.text: "'Man, 33, beaten to death in Monqiz Prison... the deceased was identified as Mateus Montalvo, a courier for the Cantuavo vineyards.'"

122.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
122.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false  and  (Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)) == false

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "Is that the man you were with in the wine cellar?"

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false  and  (Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)) == false

125.speaker: Player_Romus
125.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false  and  (Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)) == false

130.speaker: Pabel Adria
130.text: "Montalvo had recently been jailed and dismissed from his job after engaging in suspected homosexual activity with a client."

131.speaker: Player_Romus
131.text: "Oh, no. Was he arrested because of my investigation?"

132.speaker: Pabel Adria
132.text: "Our encounter was obviously neither his first nor last. I warned him to be more careful, but..."

133.speaker: Player_Romus
133.text: "This is happening in Rizia's prisons? I'll have to improve security there at once."

135.speaker: Pabel Adria
135.text: "We had an encounter some time before your coronation. Clearly neither his first nor last. I warned him to be more careful, but..."

136.speaker: Pabel Adria
136.text: "No madder than a king doing the same with his butler."

137.speaker: Pabel Adria
137.text: "Until homosexuality is no longer a crime in Rizia, people like us are going to keep dying."

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "It's a disgrace that this was allowed to occur during my reign."

141.speaker: Player_Romus
141.text: "I am working to achieve parity between commoners and nobles. I can't let the problems of a tiny minority distract me from that fight."

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: Pabel gaped at me in astonishment. A short laugh escaped his lips.

143.speaker: Pabel Adria
143.text: "You must admit it's more comfortable than that rocky cove in Monqiz."

144.speaker: Pabel Adria
144.text: "Call yourself what you want. It doesn't change the fact that in the eyes of the law, you're a criminal."

151.speaker: Player_Romus
151.text: "Your Mateus was a sinner, and so are we. I can barely stomach such behavior, let alone enshrine it into law."

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "I've been wanting to get rid of that law since I became king. But I'm afraid I don't have the authority."

153.speaker: Pabel Adria
153.text: "Rom. Any fight for equal rights should include *all* Rizians. Regardless of their romantic preferences."

154.speaker: Pabel Adria
154.text: "We're talking about basic human rights. You can't wait for the population to catch up with the times. You have to show them the way forward."

155.speaker: Player_Romus
155.text: "We shouldn't. I think Titus is starting to get suspicious."

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: He groaned quietly and withdrew his hand.

157.speaker: Player_Romus
157.text: "You missed your calling. You should've become a poet."

158.speaker: Pabel Adria
158.text: "I'd be living in the gutter. And you'd have no one to handle your... household."

163.speaker: Pabel Adria
163.text: "If you care about me -- about us -- you will find a way to make it happen."

164.speaker: Player_Romus
164.text: "There are only so many decrees I can make as king. I have to prioritize."

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "I've made so much progress for Rizia's working class. They'll see it as a betrayal of their values."

169.speaker: Player_Romus
169.text: "If I show too much sympathy towards your community, my house will never accept my plans for reform."

171.speaker: Pabel Adria
171.text: "Whose values, exactly? Working-class homosexuals are at more risk than anyone."

172.speaker: Pabel Adria
172.text: "I understand the influence Grand Wiseman Ignacius wields. But do you really plan to spend the rest of your reign catering to the Sanctuary?"

173.speaker: Player_Romus
173.text: "I'm the king. I have the authority. I can make it happen."

174.speaker: Pabel Adria
174.text: "If you care about me -- about us -- then you will."

178.speaker: Pabel Adria
178.text: "You said you felt things with me that you never felt with any woman. What kind of sick, twisted God would forbid you from that pleasure?"

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "It's not God that's sick and twisted. It's us."

180.speaker: Pabel Adria
180.text: "You said you felt things with me that you hadn't felt with anyone since Lena. What kind of sick, twisted God would forbid you from that pleasure?"

184.speaker: Player_Romus
184.text: "The same God who let the Palesians take my daughter from me."

185.speaker: Player_Romus
185.text: "The same God who took my wife away from me."

186.speaker: Player_Romus
186.text: "A truly devout Wruhecist must abandon all thoughts of earthly pleasure if he is to achieve Golconda."

190.speaker: Narrator
190.text: He stood up and brushed himself off.

191.speaker: Pabel Adria
191.text: "I care about you, Romus. I always have."

192.speaker: Pabel Adria
192.text: "But friend to friend... all this religious talk is starting to worry me."

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: He hurriedly started putting his clothes back on.

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: He put a hand on my shoulder.

195.speaker: Pabel Adria
195.text: "You're going through a hard time, I know."

196.speaker: Pabel Adria
196.text: "But you deserve love. We both do."

197.speaker: Narrator
197.text: He put a hand on my shoulder.

198.speaker: Pabel Adria
198.text: "You've gone through a hard time, I know."

202.speaker: Pabel Adria
202.text: "Or do you think a jury would let you off the hook because you're attracted to women too?"

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "I am attracted to human beings. Whether they're male or female is of no consequence."

205.speaker: Player_Romus
205.text: "I can turn it on and off, like a light switch. It's not my fault that other people can't."

206.speaker: Pabel Adria
206.text: "Plenty of your subjects feel the same way. Shouldn't the law reflect that?"

207.speaker: Pabel Adria
207.text: "It's not too late to change the law. You'd be giving so many of your subjects a chance at love. At life."

208.speaker: Player_Romus
208.text: "Changing the law would definitely give us an edge with Derdia."

212.speaker: Player_Romus
212.text: "If I show too much sympathy towards your community, my house will disown me."

215.speaker: Player_Romus
215.text: "The Dastnurists will hate it, though. What am I supposed to tell Rumburg?"

216.speaker: Pabel Adria
216.text: "Isn't Queen Beatrice a proponent of secularization? She'll understand the need to separate state laws from religious ones."

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "Still, we're in the middle of a war. It's not the time to go around making huge changes."

225.speaker: Pabel Adria
225.text: "I beg your pardon, but from what I can tell your relationship with your family is already beyond repair. What's one more burned bridge?"

226.speaker: Pabel Adria
226.text: "I know you're close with your family. But if they insist on denying us our humanity, then I'm sorry, but screw them."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "If I take this leap, my house will never forgive me."

228.speaker: Pabel Adria
228.text: "For whatever that's worth. Look at how they treat women..."

232.speaker: Pabel Adria
232.text: "I've got to go oversee breakfast. I trust you can find your own way out."

233.speaker: Pabel Adria
233.text: "There's still some time before breakfast. I suggest you go back inside and wash the sin out of your mouth."

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "We must both repent, Pabel. Before it's too late."

235.speaker: Player_Romus
235.text: "I'm sorry. I wish I could see it differently."

236.speaker: Player_Romus
236.text: "I will think about what you said. I promise."

237.speaker: Player_Romus
237.text: "Watch your own mouth. You're still speaking to the king."

238.speaker: Pabel Adria
238.text: "Don't apologize to me. Apologize to Mateus."

242.speaker: Narrator
242.text: He stood up and brushed himself off.

243.speaker: Narrator
243.text: He slowly started putting his clothes back on.

248.speaker: Pabel Adria
248.text: "He wasn't the first. And he won't be the last."

250.speaker: Narrator
250.text: He bowed and disappeared into the greenery.

251.speaker: Narrator
251.text: He turned around and swiftly disappeared into the greenery.

252.speaker: Pabel Adria
252.text: "It's too late for Mateus. But not for many others."

253.speaker: Player_Romus
253.text: "Whether or not I personally agree, classifying it as such would definitely put me on good terms with Derdia."

254.speaker: Player_Romus
254.text: "The Dastnurists would hate me if I took that leap."

255.speaker: Player_Romus
255.text: "I'm still worried about what my house will think."

256.speaker: Player_Romus
256.text: "It's not a stretch at all. Why is my butler talking more sense than my religious councilor?"

257.speaker: Pabel Adria
257.text: "Because the Grand Wiseman hasn't been intimate since before the invention of the automobile."

258.speaker: Pabel Adria
258.text: "Good thing they're still a minority here. You can afford to lose them."

259.speaker: Pabel Adria
259.text: "But yes. The Golcondists in Rizia  would also be very happy."

260.speaker: Pabel Adria
260.text: "Wow. And I thought I knew you."

261.speaker: Player_Romus
261.text: "I like guns. I'm not some nancy boy."
261.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_LovedWife"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_JoinedMilitary"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_Summer_Hugo"] == true)

265.speaker: Pabel Adria
265.text: "Really? You're going to buy into those ancient stereotypes?"

266.speaker: Player_Romus
266.text: "The working class will see it as a betrayal of their values."

267.speaker: Pabel Adria
267.text: "It's not just about you and me. This is a universal struggle. Think of the example we could set for the rest of the world."

268.speaker: Player_Romus
268.text: "I haven't seen this side of you before and frankly, I'm incredibly turned on by it."

269.speaker: Player_Romus
269.text: "I've already got my council and the House of Delegates telling me what to do. Now I have to take orders from my butler?"

270.speaker: Player_Romus
270.text: "Even if homosexuality were legal in Rizia, it doesn't mean you and I could be together openly."

271.speaker: Pabel Adria
271.text: "I know. That's a discussion for a later date."

273.speaker: Pabel Adria
273.text: "It's what happens to a man when enough of his kind are imprisoned, dead or exiled."

274.speaker: Pabel Adria
274.text: "I'm not ordering you to do anything."

275.speaker: Player_Romus
275.text: "You're right. I have a historic opportunity to change the law. I've got to seize it while I still can."

276.speaker: Pabel Adria
276.text: "The sooner you do, the more lives will be saved."

283.speaker: Narrator
283.text: He stood up and brushed himself off.

284.speaker: Narrator
284.text: He hurriedly started putting his clothes back on.

285.speaker: Pabel Adria
285.text: "I care about you, Romus. I always have."

286.speaker: Pabel Adria
286.text: "But if this isn't important to you... I don't know what to say."

287.speaker: Player_Romus
287.text: "Then keep your mouth shut. You're here to serve me, remember?"

288.speaker: Player_Romus
288.text: "It doesn't make a difference. Even if homosexuality were legal in Rizia, the people would never accept a degenerate king."

289.speaker: Narrator
289.text: He stood up and brushed himself off.

290.speaker: Narrator
290.text: He began putting his clothes back on.

291.speaker: Player_Romus
291.text: "Wait. It's important to me if it's important to you."

292.speaker: Pabel Adria
292.text: "This is more important than you or me. You could save thousands of lives."

293.speaker: Pabel Adria
293.text: "This goes beyond either of us individually. It's basic human rights."

295.speaker: Pabel Adria
295.text: "I am sorry, Your Majesty. For believing our encounters were more than an extension of my... royal duties."

296.speaker: Pabel Adria
296.text: "I know the war is your highest priority right now. But I hope you'll at least think about it."

300.speaker: Pabel Adria
300.text: "I know you have other priorities. But please just think about it."

301.speaker: Pabel Adria
301.text: "I'm late to oversee breakfast. I trust you can find your own way out."

302.speaker: Player_Romus
302.text: "Not unless you write me another poem."

306.speaker: Pabel Adria
306.text: "Please forgive my confusion, Your Majesty. I wasn't the one on my knees a moment ago."

307.speaker: Pabel Adria
307.text: "I'm late to oversee breakfast. I trust you can find your own way out."

308.speaker: Narrator
308.text: He bowed and swiftly disappeared into the greenery.

312.speaker: Narrator
312.text: After collecting my thoughts, I dressed and left the maze the way I'd come.

313.speaker: Narrator
313.text: After collecting my thoughts, I stood and left the maze the way I'd come.

317.speaker: Narrator
317.text: Bruno ran towards me as soon as I emerged. Together, we began the walk back to the palace.

318.speaker: Narrator
318.text: I emerged by the willow trees and began the walk back to the palace.

319.speaker: Pabel Adria
319.text: "But if this isn't important to you... I don't know what to say."

323.speaker: Narrator
323.text: He stood up and brushed himself off.

324.speaker: Narrator
324.text: He hurriedly started putting his clothes back on.

325.speaker: Player_Romus
325.text: "It's important to me. But it won't happen overnight."

327.speaker: Player_Romus
327.text: "My child might die. That's what's important to me right now."

331.speaker: Player_Romus
331.text: "Is that why you're with me? To push your... lavender agenda?"

332.speaker: Pabel Adria
332.text: "I know. But Mateus was someone's child, too."

336.speaker: Player_Romus
336.text: "I'll look into making a decree. I promise."

339.speaker: Pabel Adria
339.text: "My creative muscles are spent. Just look for the willows."

342.speaker: Pabel Adria
342.text: "It's not an agenda. It's a crisis. How many more of us have to die before you see it the same way?"

344.speaker: Narrator
344.text: He leaned down and kissed me, then swiftly disappeared into the greenery.

349.speaker: Narrator
349.text: Early in the morning, I heard a soft tap on the door to my bedchambers.

350.speaker: Narrator
350.text: It was Pabel, coming to wake me at my usual time.

354.speaker: Narrator
354.text: Bruno ran up to him with a gleeful wag of his tail.

355.speaker: Pabel Adria
355.text: "What a happy fellow. I hope you both slept well."

356.speaker: Narrator
356.text: There was a tinge of melancholy in his voice.

357.speaker: Pabel Adria
357.text: "Good morning, {RiziaDLCText.PabelToPlayer}. I hope you slept well."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "What's going on, Pabel? Are you all right?"

364.speaker: Player_Romus
364.text: "I won't sleep until we take Pales."

365.speaker: Player_Romus
365.text: "I won't sleep until we have Zille back."

366.speaker: Pabel Adria
366.text: "I have it. Just give me one moment."

369.speaker: Pabel Adria
369.text: "Even a king needs to close his eyes sometimes. I'll ask the pharmacist to procure you some Wehzek tablets."

370.speaker: Narrator
370.text: He began drawing open my curtains, then stopped and spoke to me in a forced casual tone.

371.speaker: Pabel Adria
371.text: "How are preparations going for your royal visit to Derdia?"

372.speaker: Player_Romus
372.text: "To the land of blasphemous lunatics, you mean? I couldn't be more excited."

377.speaker: Narrator
377.text: He paused again, as if in deliberation. Finally, he walked over to the chair next to my bed and sat down.

378.speaker: Pabel Adria
378.text: "I don't know if you're aware, but many Rizians of my persuasion have fled to Derdia since its establishment as a Golcondist republic."

379.speaker: Pabel Adria
379.text: "It's not perfect. But I understand the desire to live openly among fundamentalists rather than cower behind closed doors."

380.speaker: Player_Romus
380.text: "It can't be that bad in Rizia. Can it?"

381.speaker: Player_Romus
381.text: "Really? I thought the lure of the forbidden was part of your whole... thing."

382.speaker: Pabel Adria
382.text: "You don't know the half of it."

385.speaker: Pabel Adria
385.text: "It's not a game, {RiziaDLCText.PabelToPlayer}. It's who we are."

387.speaker: Player_Romus
387.text: "Something must be done to improve the status of your kind here at home."

393.speaker: Player_Romus
393.text: "I've been reading up on the Golcondists. Perhaps Rizia has been too harsh to judge them in the past."

397.speaker: Player_Romus
397.text: "I don't have high hopes, to be honest. The Derdians and I have nothing in common."

398.speaker: Player_Romus
398.text: "They are going well, thank you. I'm hoping to contract their mercenaries for the war."

399.speaker: Pabel Adria
399.text: "You know what they say about opposites attracting, Your Majesty."

400.speaker: Pabel Adria
400.text: "'Man, 33, beaten to death in Monqiz Prison... the deceased was identified as Mateus Montalvo, a courier for the Cantuavo vineyards.'"

401.speaker: Pabel Adria
401.text: "Montalvo had recently been jailed and dismissed from his job after engaging in suspected homosexual activity with a client."

402.speaker: Player_Romus
402.text: "I've got high hopes for it. The Derdians and I agree on many points."

403.speaker: Pabel Adria
403.text: "I see. I've heard they're very skilled fighters."

404.speaker: Narrator
404.text: He tossed the morning paper onto my bed.

405.speaker: Pabel Adria
405.text: "Look at the bottom of the first page."

408.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
408.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false) == false

409.speaker: Player_Romus
409.text: "Is that the man you were with in the wine cellar? Allegedly, I mean."

410.speaker: Player_Romus
410.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false) == false

411.speaker: Player_Romus
411.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false) == false

416.speaker: Player_Romus
416.text: "Oh, no. Was he arrested because of my investigation?"

417.speaker: Pabel Adria
417.text: "Our encounter was obviously neither his first nor last. I warned him to be more careful, but..."

418.speaker: Player_Romus
418.text: "This is happening in Rizia's prisons? I'll have to improve security there at once."

420.speaker: Pabel Adria
420.text: "We had an encounter some time before your coronation. Clearly neither his first nor last. I warned him to be more careful, but..."

421.speaker: Pabel Adria
421.text: "If he's mad, then so am I."

422.speaker: Pabel Adria
422.text: "Until homosexuality is no longer a crime in Rizia, people like him -- like me -- are going to keep dying."

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "It's a disgrace that this happened during my reign."

425.speaker: Pabel Adria
425.text: "He wasn't the first. And he won't be the last."

426.speaker: Player_Romus
426.text: "Relax. I'm the king. If you ever get found out, I'll just pardon you."

427.speaker: Player_Romus
427.text: "I am working to achieve parity between commoners and nobles. I can't let the problems of a tiny minority distract me from that fight."

428.speaker: Narrator
428.text: Pabel gave me a look of frustration.

429.speaker: Player_Romus
429.text: "If the people of Rizia wanted legal homosexuality, my parliament would have brought it up by now."

430.speaker: Pabel Adria
430.text: "That's very kind of you, but there are thousands like me in this kingdom. And they count as some of its most vulnerable citizens."

437.speaker: Player_Romus
437.text: "Your Mateus was a sinner, and so are you. I can barely stomach such behavior, let alone enshrine it into law."

438.speaker: Player_Romus
438.text: "I've been wanting to get rid of that law since I became king. But I'm afraid it's going to take more resources than I have."

439.speaker: Pabel Adria
439.text: "Any fight for equal rights should include *all* Rizians. Regardless of their romantic preferences."

440.speaker: Pabel Adria
440.text: "This is one instance where democracy doesn't work. You can't wait for the population to catch up with the times. You have to show them the way forward."

445.speaker: Pabel Adria
445.text: "It is a challenge, I know. Not even Queen Lyza dared to imagine it."

446.speaker: Player_Romus
446.text: "There are only so many royal decrees I can make. I have to prioritize."

447.speaker: Player_Romus
447.text: "I've made so much progress for Rizia's working class. They'll see it as a betrayal of their values."

451.speaker: Player_Romus
451.text: "If I show too much sympathy towards your community, my house will never accept my plans for reform."

452.speaker: Pabel Adria
452.text: "Whose values? Working-class homosexuals are at more risk than nearly anyone else in Rizia."

453.speaker: Player_Romus
453.text: "Rizia is still a majority-Wruhecist country. If I made homosexuality legal, the religious backlash could end my reign."

454.speaker: Pabel Adria
454.text: "I understand the influence Grand Wiseman Ignacius wields. But do you really plan to spend the rest of your reign catering to the Sanctuary?"

455.speaker: Player_Romus
455.text: "I have the authority. I can change our kingdom's anti-homosexuality laws."

456.speaker: Pabel Adria
456.text: "It's a major step forward, I know. Not even Queen Lyza dared to imagine it."

457.speaker: Pabel Adria
457.text: "What kind of sick, twisted God would forbid a person from experiencing love?"

458.speaker: Player_Romus
458.text: "It's not God that's sick and twisted. It's you. No offense."

459.speaker: Player_Romus
459.text: "It is true that Wruhecist teachings stress the importance of bringing joy to others. They do not specify which sex."

463.speaker: Player_Romus
463.text: "The same God who let the Palesians take my daughter from me."

464.speaker: Player_Romus
464.text: "The same God who took my wife away from me."

466.speaker: Pabel Adria
466.text: "You're going through a hard time, I know."

469.speaker: Pabel Adria
469.text: "You've gone through a hard time, I know."

471.speaker: Pabel Adria
471.text: "Is it such a stretch to imagine that a bond of affection between two men can be as pure -- as holy -- as that between a man and a woman?"

472.speaker: Pabel Adria
472.text: "Then as your friend, I beg of you. Prioritize this one."

477.speaker: Pabel Adria
477.text: "Your approval means as much to House Toras as theirs means to you. They can be won over."

478.speaker: Player_Romus
478.text: "Rizia may be ready, but House Toras is not."

479.speaker: Pabel Adria
479.text: "I've got to go oversee breakfast. I'll leave you to dress yourself."

482.speaker: Player_Romus
482.text: "Personally, I would rather not imagine it. But politically, it'd give us an edge with Derdia."

483.speaker: Player_Romus
483.text: "The Dastnurists would hate me if I took that leap."

484.speaker: Player_Romus
484.text: "I'm still worried about what my house will think."

485.speaker: Player_Romus
485.text: "It's not a stretch at all. Why is my butler talking more sense than my religious councilor?"

486.speaker: Pabel Adria
486.text: "Because the Grand Wiseman hasn't been intimate since before the invention of the automobile."

487.speaker: Pabel Adria
487.text: "They are still a minority here. You can afford to lose them."

488.speaker: Pabel Adria
488.text: "But that's not the real reason the law should be changed."

489.speaker: Pabel Adria
489.text: "It's not just about what I want. This is a universal struggle. Think of the example you'd be setting for the rest of the world."

490.speaker: Player_Romus
490.text: "A truly devout Wruhecist must abandon all thoughts of earthly pleasure if he is to achieve Golconda."

491.speaker: Pabel Adria
491.text: "But friend to friend... all this religious talk is starting to worry me."

492.speaker: Player_Romus
492.text: "Decriminalizing homosexuality will definitely give us an edge with Derdia."

493.speaker: Pabel Adria
493.text: "I care about you, Romus. I always have."

494.speaker: Player_Romus
494.text: "If I show too much sympathy towards your community, my house will disown me."

498.speaker: Pabel Adria
498.text: "I beg your pardon, but from what I can tell your relationship with your family is already beyond repair. What's one more burned bridge?"

499.speaker: Player_Romus
499.text: "The Dastnurists will hate it, though. What am I supposed to tell Rumburg?"

500.speaker: Pabel Adria
500.text: "Isn't Queen Beatrice a proponent of secularization? She'll understand the need to separate state laws from religious ones."

501.speaker: Player_Romus
501.text: "Still, we're in the middle of a war. It's not the time to go around making huge changes."

502.speaker: Player_Romus
502.text: "I will think about what you said. I promise."

504.speaker: Pabel Adria
504.text: "As well as with the Golcondists living here in Rizia."

505.speaker: Player_Romus
505.text: "You shouldn't be worried. I am seeing clearly for the first time in my life."

506.speaker: Pabel Adria
506.text: "Then why can't you see homosexuals as people?"

507.speaker: Pabel Adria
507.text: "Pardon my frustration. I'll see you shortly."

508.speaker: Narrator
508.text: He bowed and swiftly left the room.

509.speaker: Pabel Adria
509.text: "It's too late for Mateus. But not for many others."

510.speaker: Player_Romus
510.text: "I'm sorry. I wish I could see it differently."

511.speaker: Pabel Adria
511.text: "Don't apologize to me. Apologize to Mateus."

512.speaker: Player_Romus
512.text: "The working class will see it as a betrayal of their values."

514.speaker: Pabel Adria
514.text: "I am sorry, Your Majesty. I was mistaken to conflate our past friendship with our professional relationship."

519.speaker: Player_Romus
519.text: "My child might die. That's what's important to me right now."

523.speaker: Pabel Adria
523.text: "It's not an agenda. It's a crisis. How many more of us have to die before you see it the same way?"

524.speaker: Narrator
524.text: He bowed and swiftly left the room.

525.speaker: Narrator
525.text: He bowed and swiftly left the room.

528.speaker: Player_Romus
528.text: "I'll look into making a decree. I promise."

531.speaker: Pabel Adria
531.text: "I'm late to oversee breakfast. I'll leave you to dress yourself."

532.speaker: Pabel Adria
532.text: "I'm so sorry, Your Majesty. I won't bring up personal topics with you again."

533.speaker: Pabel Adria
533.text: "I'm late to oversee breakfast. I'll leave you to dress yourself."

534.speaker: Player_Romus
534.text: "I've already got my council and the House of Delegates telling me what to do. Now I have to take orders from my butler?"

535.speaker: Player_Romus
535.text: "Even if I made homosexuality legal tomorrow, you couldn't go parading about town in a ball gown. Royal protocol must be observed."

536.speaker: Pabel Adria
536.text: "I assure you I will be as discreet as ever. I will merely be happy to see fewer of my kind imprisoned, killed or exiled."

537.speaker: Player_Romus
537.text: "You're right. I have a historic opportunity. I've got to seize it while I still can."

538.speaker: Pabel Adria
538.text: "The sooner you do, the more lives will be saved."

540.speaker: Player_Romus
540.text: "Then keep your mouth shut. You're my servant, remember?"

541.speaker: Pabel Adria
541.text: "But if this isn't important to you... I don't know what to say."

542.speaker: Player_Romus
542.text: "It's important to me. But it won't happen overnight."

546.speaker: Player_Romus
546.text: "Is that why you worked your way up to head butler? To push your... lavender agenda?"

550.speaker: Player_Romus
550.text: "Plenty of people don't get to experience love. I didn't."

551.speaker: Pabel Adria
551.text: "That's not a reason to deny it to others."

552.speaker: Pabel Adria
552.text: "But remember the joy you experienced during your marriage to Princess Lena. Shouldn't everyone get a chance at that, even if it ends in heartbreak?"

557.speaker: Pabel Adria
557.text: "I shouldn't have brought this up with you, Your Majesty."

559.speaker: Player_Romus
559.text: "I will gladly forget it. And I'll thank you not to trouble me with such talk again."

560.speaker: Pabel Adria
560.text: "I've got to go oversee breakfast. I'll leave you to dress yourself."

562.speaker: Player_Romus
562.text: "If I show too much sympathy towards your community, my house will disown me."

563.speaker: Player_Romus
563.text: "There are only so many decrees I can make. I have to prioritize."

564.speaker: Player_Romus
564.text: "They can move to Derdia. You said it's safe for them there, right?"

565.speaker: Pabel Adria
565.text: "Not everyone has the resources to flee the country. And living as a Golcondist is hardly an ideal solution, anyway."

570.speaker: Pabel Adria
570.text: "I'm grateful that you respect my identity, Your Majesty."

571.speaker: Pabel Adria
571.text: "But if the lives of other homosexuals in Rizia aren't important to you... I don't know what to say."

572.speaker: Pabel Adria
572.text: "I care about you, Romus. I always have."

573.speaker: Player_Romus
573.text: "They are important to me. But I can't make change happen overnight."

581.speaker: Pabel Adria
581.text: "Navy blue suit, burgundy pocket square. The diamond cuff links Hugo gave you for your birthday."

582.speaker: Narrator
582.text: After taking a moment to collect my thoughts, I dressed and headed downstairs for breakfast.

583.speaker: Pabel Adria
583.text: "He wasn't my lover. But I'm sorry too."

587.speaker: Pabel Adria
587.text: "Even a king needs to close his eyes sometimes. I'll ask the chef to procure some valerian root for tea."

591.speaker: Player_Romus
591.text: "They are going well, thank you. I'm hoping to contract their mercenaries for use in Zille."

593.speaker: Pabel Adria
593.text: "It's one of the only places in Merkopa where relations between members of the same sex are accepted."

594.speaker: Player_Romus
594.text: "One of the many perversions of Golcondism."

598.speaker: Player_Romus
598.text: "Are you saying that in some respects, Golcondists are more enlightened than mainstream Wruhecists?"

599.speaker: Player_Romus
599.text: "A fascinating contradiction. How can such an extremist society allow homosexuality?"

601.speaker: Pabel Adria
601.text: "The only reason Derdia allows homosexuality is because Golcondists view intimacy between men as the most sacred form of love. They say it strengthens bonds on the battlefield."

602.speaker: Player_Romus
602.text: "It could greatly improve our image in the war. A kingdom that grants rights to women and homosexuals can't be an aggressor."

606.speaker: Pabel Adria
606.text: "And not all homosexual men wear  gowns. Just as not all men who wear gowns are homosexual."

611.speaker: Pabel Adria
611.text: "Then as your butler and humble subject, I beg of you. Prioritize this one."

613.speaker: Pabel Adria
613.text: "As for women... as long as they accept their role as providers and childbearers, they may consort among themselves if they wish."

615.speaker: Player_Romus
615.text: "To the land of blasphemous lunatics, you mean? I couldn't be more excited."

616.speaker: Pabel Adria
616.text: "Not all of their beliefs are crazy."

617.speaker: Narrator
617.text: He paused. I saw a flash of melancholy in his eyes.

618.speaker: Pabel Adria
618.text: "I don't know if you're aware, but many Rizians of my persuasion have fled to Derdia since its establishment as a Golcondist republic."

619.speaker: Pabel Adria
619.text: "It's not perfect. But I understand the desire to live openly among fundamentalists rather than cower behind closed doors."

620.speaker: Player_Romus
620.text: "It can't be that bad in Rizia. Can it?"

621.speaker: Player_Romus
621.text: "Derdia's attitude towards homosexuality is just an extension of the deep-seated sexism in its society. How could anyone prefer that to our kingdom?"

622.speaker: Player_Romus
622.text: "Boring. Without the lure of the forbidden, I might as well be with a woman."

623.speaker: Pabel Adria
623.text: "You don't know the half of it."

626.speaker: Pabel Adria
626.text: "Do you mean that, Romus? Is this a game to you?"

627.speaker: Pabel Adria
627.text: "Because of what our kingdom does to homosexuals who get caught."

629.speaker: Player_Romus
629.text: "So do I. They should never have had to flee Rizia."

630.speaker: Pabel Adria
630.text: "And those who fled are the lucky ones."

634.speaker: Player_Romus
634.text: "Aha. You're jealous that I get to go to the homosexual country and you don't."

638.speaker: Player_Romus
638.text: "I don't have high hopes, to be honest. The Derdians and I have nothing in common."

639.speaker: Player_Romus
639.text: "As well as can be expected. I'm hoping to contract their mercenaries for the war."

641.speaker: Player_Romus
641.text: "I've got high hopes for it. The Derdians and I agree on many points."

642.speaker: Pabel Adria
642.text: "Ah. I've heard they're very skilled fighters."

644.speaker: Player_Romus
644.text: "As well as can be expected. I'm hoping to contract their mercenaries for use in Zille."

646.speaker: Pabel Adria
646.text: "It's one of the only places in Merkopa where relations between members of the same sex are accepted."

647.speaker: Player_Romus
647.text: "One of the many perversions of Golcondism."

651.speaker: Player_Romus
651.text: "Are you saying that in some respects, Golcondists are more enlightened than mainstream Wruhecists?"

652.speaker: Player_Romus
652.text: "A fascinating contradiction. How can such an extremist society allow homosexuality?"

654.speaker: Pabel Adria
654.text: "The only reason homosexuality is allowed in Derdia is because Golcondists view intimacy between men as the most sacred form of love. They say it strengthens bonds on the battlefield."

655.speaker: Pabel Adria
655.text: "And leave my king? Never. But I do sometimes wonder what such a society is like."

656.speaker: Pabel Adria
656.text: "As for women... as long as they accept their role as providers and childbearers, they may consort among themselves if they wish."

657.speaker: Player_Romus
657.text: "I would love to permit such a thing in Rizia, but I'd lose the throne in an instant. All of society is against it."

658.speaker: Pabel Adria
658.text: "To be fair, the Derdians are far from enlightened."

659.speaker: Player_Romus
659.text: "It is true that Wruhecist teachings stress the importance of bringing joy to others. They do not specify which sex."

661.speaker: Pabel Adria
661.text: "Is it really such a stretch to imagine that the love between two men can be as pure -- as holy -- as that between members of the opposite sex?"

665.speaker: Pabel Adria
665.text: "Exactly. And don't even try to tell me I didn't bring joy to you just now."

669.speaker: Narrator
669.text: Pabel put a hand on my shoulder.

672.speaker: Pabel Adria
672.text: "Since when is what we're doing a perversion?"

677.speaker: Player_Romus
677.text: "You're talking about a tiny minority of citizens. Why cater to them at the expense of everyone else?"

678.speaker: Pabel Adria
678.text: "Why would it have to be at anyone's expense? Who are we hurting?"

682.speaker: Pabel Adria
682.text: "You know very well that your parliament only puts forth the interests of the nobility. Who can afford to keep their perversions hidden away."

686.speaker: Player_Romus
686.text: "If Rizia wanted legal homosexuality, my parliament would have brought it up by now."

690.speaker: Pabel Adria
690.text: "You know very well that your parliament only puts forth the interests of the nobility. Who can afford to keep their perversions hidden away."

694.speaker: Player_Romus
694.text: "Rizia is still a majority-Wruhecist country. If I made homosexuality legal, the religious backlash could end my reign."

695.speaker: Player_Romus
695.text: "People like us represent a tiny minority of citizens. Why focus on them at the expense of everyone else?"

696.speaker: Pabel Adria
696.text: "Why would it have to be at anyone's expense? Who are we hurting?"

697.speaker: Player_Romus
697.text: "Derdia's attitude towards homosexuality is just an extension of the deep-seated sexism in its society. How could anyone prefer that to our kingdom?"

698.speaker: Pabel Adria
698.text: "Because of what our kingdom does to homosexuals who get caught."

702.speaker: Pabel Adria
702.text: "Palace scuttlebutt has it you turned down the chance to visit Derdia."

703.speaker: Player_Romus
703.text: "Why do you care about my diplomatic dealings?"

704.speaker: Pabel Adria
704.text: "I know it's not my business. But I would have been curious to hear what you thought of the place."

705.speaker: Player_Romus
705.text: "Yes, I don't want to have any more contact with those lunatics than I need to."

706.speaker: Pabel Adria
706.text: "Understandable. But I would have been curious to hear what you thought of the place."

707.speaker: Player_Romus
707.text: "It would have been a waste of time. Rizia's place is among the monarchies of GRACE, not scrabbling for favor with our neighbors."

711.speaker: Player_Romus
711.text: "It would've been counterproductive. I'll have better relations with our other international partners if I avoid Derdia."

712.speaker: Pabel Adria
712.text: "I see. Still, I would have been curious what you thought of the place."

713.speaker: Player_Romus
713.text: "Yes, and I'm regretting it now. I'd be interested in seeing how they live over there."

723.speaker: Player_Romus
723.text: "Accepted and condoned. Sal told me all about this."

724.speaker: Pabel Adria
724.text: "With a judgemental scowl on his face, no doubt."

725.speaker: Pabel Adria
725.text: "I don't agree with Derdia's religious justification for homosexuality. And I certainly don't like their martial culture."

726.speaker: Pabel Adria
726.text: "But I understand the desire to live openly among fundamentalists rather than cower behind closed doors."

752.text: "Since when do you care about my diplomatic dealings?"

753.speaker: Pabel Adria
753.text: "I don't, usually. But this one is different."

754.speaker: Player_Romus
754.text: "You should be glad. What if I went there and some handsome, virile Golcondist warrior swept me off my feet?"

755.speaker: Pabel Adria
755.text: "At least neither of you would be jailed for it."

760.speaker: Player_Romus
760.text: "Accepted and condoned. Sal told me all about this."
